Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
Comments: No authoritative government e-filing “tax portal” evidence located in sources reviewed; the most concrete evidence relates to mobile tax payments and bank portal payments rather than a national e-filing portal. Searches included Liberia Revenue Authority “e-filing”, “tax portal”, and “online filing”, but did not yield a credible official portal reference in retrieved sources.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A light-touch fast-path check surfaced a clearly authoritative, on-point source (the Liberia Revenue Authority's own website), so the row was escalated to the full verification path rather than confirmed as Unknown. Fetched pages confirm the LRA operates an official eServices/eFiling portal built around the Liberia Integrated Tax System (LITAS), offering online tax return filing, a 'Pay Tax Here' e-payment gateway, and POS/bank-transfer/Visa card payments — this has existed since at least 2020. However, the variable specifically asks whether the portal's e-payment capability is linked to the instant payment system (NEPS/IIPS). The Central Bank of Liberia's directive of 23 September 2025 mandates that Person-to-Government (P2G) revenue collections via mobile money be routed exclusively through NEPS/IIPS from 1 December 2025, and an 18 December 2025 news report on the IIPS launch states that 'work is ongoing with the Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA) to roll out People-to-Government (P2G) payments, allowing citizens to pay taxes digitally' — indicating the NEPS-linked integration was still being rolled out rather than fully live. Value Code recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 3 (Under development): a functioning tax e-filing/e-payment portal exists, but its integration with the instant payment system is in progress rather than complete.
revised_comments: The Liberia Revenue Authority operates an official online tax portal (eServices/eFiling, built on the Liberia Integrated Tax System, LITAS) allowing taxpayers to file returns and pay taxes and customs duties online via bank transfer, Visa card and POS. Integration of this portal's e-payments with the Central Bank of Liberia's new instant payment system (NEPS/IIPS) is under active development: a September 2025 CBL directive mandates that government revenue collections via mobile money be routed through NEPS/IIPS from December 2025, and implementation with the LRA was reported as ongoing in December 2025.

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: Government payment digitization share not found as a quantified percentage; evidence only indicates IIPS supports G2P (salaries/social benefits) and that government is pursuing digitization. Without a measured proportion of government payments digitized, score kept as unknown.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A light-touch fast-path search surfaced clearly authoritative, on-point evidence, so the row was escalated to the full path rather than confirmed Unknown. A Central Bank of Liberia directive (23 September 2025) mandates that ALL government-to-person payments (salaries, pensions, social benefits, other transfers) made via mobile money be routed exclusively through NEPS/IIPS from 27 October 2025, and that all government revenue collections (P2G) via mobile money be routed through NEPS/IIPS from 1 December 2025 — a binding regulatory mandate for full digitisation of G2P mobile-money flows. Concrete implementation data corroborates substantial progress: as of the reported Phase 1 rollout, approximately 38,000 of Liberia's roughly 50,000 civil servants (about 76%) in Montserrado, Margibi and Grand Bassa counties now receive salaries via mobile money, with Phase 2 (remaining counties) still pending. Because this figure covers only the salary component of G2P (not pensions or social transfers specifically), and because the CBL mandate reflects intent/rules rather than a directly measured aggregate percentage across all G2P categories, the recalculated Value Code of 3 (50-69%) is a considered estimate rather than a precise figure and is flagged for human review to confirm whether pensions/social transfers digitisation is comparable to the salary figure.
revised_comments: Liberia is in an active, government-mandated transition of G2P disbursements to digital instant payments. A Central Bank of Liberia directive requires all mobile-money-based government-to-person payments (salaries, pensions, social benefits) to route through the national instant payment system (NEPS/IIPS) from October 2025. In the first implementation phase, around 76% of civil servants (approximately 38,000 of 50,000), located in Montserrado, Margibi and Grand Bassa counties, now receive salaries via mobile money rather than cash, with a further rollout phase planned for remaining counties.
